title: When does a noisy Bell pair attain the Rains bound?
problem: Two qubits sharing a Bell pair hit by unknown Pauli errors form a Bell-diagonal state \(\rho=\sum_ip_iB_i\). The best upper bound on how much entanglement can be distilled from many copies, the Rains bound, equals \(1-h_2(F)\), where \(F\) is the largest Bell probability, whatever the other three probabilities are. Is this bound attained by operations preserving the positive partial transpose (PPT), which include all LOCC protocols, and so does the bound decide the two-way quantum capacity of Pauli channels such as the depolarizing channel?
result: For entangled Bell-diagonal qubit states, PPT-preserving distillation attains the Rains bound \(1-h_2(F)\) exactly when one of the four Bell probabilities is zero, and falls strictly below it when all four are positive. Every mixed entangled isotropic state in every finite dimension also falls strictly below its bound. Hence the two-way quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel lies strictly below the Pirandola–Laurenza–Ottaviani–Banchi relative-entropy bound for all \(1/2<F<1\); at \(F=3/4\) the certified interval is \(0.18355862\le Q_{\rm PPT}<0.188642407\) against \(1-h_2(3/4)=0.18872\).
significance: Two states with the same Rains bound behave differently, so the bound cannot be the distillable entanglement in general, even for the simplest noisy Bell pairs. The result corrects an attainment conjecture drawn from finite-block numerics and gives the first proof that the depolarizing channel's two-way capacity is strictly below its relative-entropy bound, while other channels (thermal loss, amplifier, additive noise) attain theirs. The converse technique, harmonic measure applied to a complex pencil of states, is new and may apply to other strict-gap questions.
limitations: The gaps proved are small, between \(7.9\times10^{-5}\) and \(5.2\times10^{-3}\) ebits per pair at \(F=3/4\), and the paper does not give the exact rates. Attainment on the rank-three face is shown for PPT-preserving operations, not for LOCC. The numerical intervals rely on finite witnesses and certificates supplied in ancillary files, which were not checked here. The authors state that GPT-6 Astra generated candidate derivations and proofs and that Claude Opus 5.5 checked derivations and references, and that they examined and revised all results.

methods_source_section: “Using an absent error” (Eqs. (3)–(4)); “Why full support prevents attainment” (Eqs. (5)–(8)); “Isotropic states”; “Channel consequences” (Eq. (10))
methods_basis: Based on the linked paper version. Derivations marked as editorial, and suggested uses in other problems, are editorial guidance rather than results of the paper.
description: Label the Bell projectors so that \(p_0=F\) is the largest probability. The Rains bound, the minimum relative entropy to operators whose partial transpose has trace norm at most one, equals \(U=1-h_2(F)\) for every Bell-diagonal qubit state with \(F>1/2\), and so does the relative entropy of entanglement, even regularized. It cannot tell a source with one kind of Pauli error from one with three. With a single kind of error the problem reduces to dephasing, and hashing attains \(U\). The question is what happens with two or three kinds.

PPT-preserving operations are completely positive maps that remain completely positive after conjugation by the partial transpose. They contain every LOCC protocol, and Rains showed that their best fidelity with a \(K\)-dimensional maximally entangled state on \(n\) copies is the maximum of \(\mathrm{Tr}(T\rho^{\otimes n})\) over \(0\le T\le I\) with \(\|T^\Gamma\|_\infty\le1/K\). The paper uses this single test in both directions.

With two error types present, an effect that also uses the empty Bell label meets the test with exactly the right transposed norm, so PPT operations distill at \(U\). With all three present, the authors prove a strict gap: at rates above some \(U-\Delta\) with \(\Delta>0\), every PPT protocol has exponentially small fidelity. The same holds for isotropic states in any dimension, refuting attainment suggested by linear programmes on up to 100 copies.

Through teleportation, the qubit Pauli channel with Choi state \(\rho\) has PPT-assisted capacity equal to \(D_{\rm PPT}(\rho)\). A Pauli channel with one Pauli error missing therefore has PPT-assisted capacity exactly \(1-h_2(F)\), and the depolarizing channel lies strictly below its PLOB bound. The authors' own LOCC lookahead protocol reaches about \(0.088\) ebits per use at \(F=3/4\), far below both.

methods.technique: Using an empty Bell label to meet Rains' test exactly
methods.explanation: Rains' test asks for an effect with large expectation on the input and small transposed norm. When one Bell label carries no probability, the effect can be modified on that label without changing what it measures on the input, and the modification can be tuned to make the transposed norm exactly what a likelihood-ratio test needs.
math: Let \(p_3=0\), \(e=1-F\) and \(s=e/F\). The effects \[G=B_0+sB_3,\qquad A=B_1+B_2,\qquad Z=(1-s)B_3\] sum to the identity and have probabilities \(F\), \(e\) and \(0\). The partial transposes of the Bell projectors are \(B_i^\Gamma=I/2-\Pi_i\) with orthogonal rank-one \(\Pi_i\), and evaluating on these gives \[2F\,|G^\Gamma|+2e\,|A^\Gamma|=I.\] Editorial check: the identity holds numerically to \(3\times10^{-16}\) at \(F=0.6\), \(0.75\) and \(0.9\).

On \(n\) copies, sum the product effects whose score product, with scores \(2F\), \(2e\), \(0\), is at least \(2^{nR}\). Tensoring the identity and applying the triangle inequality eigenvalue by eigenvalue bounds the partial transpose of this sum between \(\pm2^{-nR}I\), which meets Rains' test with \(K=2^{nR}\). By the law of large numbers the expectation tends to one whenever \(R<F\log_2(2F)+e\log_2(2e)=1-h_2(F)\).

The construction does not care how \(e\) splits between \(B_1\) and \(B_2\), which is why every state on the rank-three face attains the bound. Editorial remark: the individual outcomes \(G,A,Z\) need not be implementable by LOCC; only the final thresholded test has to define a PPT map.
methods.transfer: Freedom outside the support of the input can be spent on satisfying an operator-norm constraint without changing statistics on the input. The same device may tighten other semidefinite converses that involve partial transposes or other positivity constraints.

methods.technique: A complex pencil of states and harmonic measure for a strict converse
methods.explanation: To show that no protocol reaches the bound when all labels are present, the authors embed the input in a one-parameter family of operators and study a polynomial built from any candidate test. Bounds at the physical point and at a separable point, plus Rains' constraint at complex points, are combined by potential theory into a deficit that does not shrink with the block length.
math: For a test \(T\), set \(P_n(z)=e^{n\mathcal U}\mathrm{Tr}\bigl[T\bigl((B_0+z\sigma)/2\bigr)^{\otimes n}\bigr]\), where \(\sigma\) is the normalized error part and \(\mathcal U=U\ln2\). At \(z=s\) the pencil is proportional to the input; at \(z=1\) it is the separable comparator. Rains' constraint gives, at every complex \(z\), \(n^{-1}\ln|P_n(z)|\le\beta+\ln H(z)\) with \[H(z)=\tfrac14\Bigl(|z-1|+\sum_{i=1}^3|1+(1-2v_i)z|\Bigr).\]

At \(z=-1\) the four moduli are \(2,2v_1,2v_2,2v_3\) and \(H(-1)=1\). If all \(v_i>0\), \(H\) is smooth there, with \(H(-1+\xi)\le1+C|\xi|^2\) and \(C=(\sum_iv_i^{-1}-7)/16\); if some \(v_i=0\), a modulus has its corner at \(-1\) and the quadratic estimate fails. Editorial check: for \(v=(0.5,0.3,0.2)\), \(C=0.2083\) and \(1+C\cdot0.05^2=1.000520\) matches the directly computed \(H(-1+0.05i)\) to six digits.

Averaging the subharmonic function \(u_n(z)=n^{-1}\ln|P_n(z)|-e\ln|z|\) over small circles near \(-1\) gains a first-order term \(eb/\pi\) against a second-order loss, so \(u_n\le\beta_+-\gamma\) on an arc of positive length. Harmonic measure transports this deficit to the physical point \(z=\sqrt s\), and concentration of the error count forces \(u_n(\sqrt s)\ge-o(1)\) for any protocol with fidelity bounded away from zero. Together these give \(D_{\rm PPT}\le U-2\gamma\omega/\ln2\), with \(\omega\) the harmonic measure of the arc.
methods.transfer: Turning a family of states into a polynomial in a complex parameter lets constraints that hold off the physical line inform the physical point, through the maximum principle and harmonic measure. This is a general route to strict converses where entropic bounds are tight to first order.
